We are a team of enthusiastic first-year B.Tech students specialising in AI & Machine Learning. Our interests include artificial intelligence, web development, Python, problem-solving, space science and innovative technology. Our team has experience with Python, AI/ML, APIs, dashboards, website development, research and presentations.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are working on the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, an interactive educational game
summary:
**Project Title: Lunar Outpost – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer**

Lunar Outpost is an interactive educational game designed to introduce students to the challenges of living and working on the Moon. Players take on the role of junior astronauts responsible for managing a simulated lunar research outpost. Through interactive training sessions and mission-based challenges, they learn about life-support systems, oxygen and water management, solar power, radiation protection, food production and lunar exploration.

The game addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by transforming complex space science and mission-planning concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience. Players make decisions, manage limited resources and observe how their choices affect mission progress and crew safety.

Our goal is to inspire students to explore space science, develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills, understand the challenges of future lunar missions, and encourage the next generation of space explorers.
details:
Project Details: Lunar Outpost – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Lunar Outpost – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational game that introduces students to the challenges of living and working on the Moon. Players take on the role of junior astronauts responsible for operating a simulated lunar research outpost. They complete training activities and mission-based challenges involving life-support systems, oxygen and water management, energy conservation, radiation protection, food production, and lunar exploration.

The project works through an interactive simulation in which players make decisions, manage limited resources, respond to mission events, and observe the consequences of their choices. This approach helps learners understand how different systems in a lunar habitat depend on one another and why teamwork, planning, and resource management are essential for successful space missions.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
The project makes complex space-science concepts easier and more engaging for students. It encourages curiosity about space exploration while developing critical thinking, problem-solving, decision-making, and resource-management skills. Our intended impact is to make space education more accessible and inspire students to explore STEM subjects and future opportunities in space science and technology.

Tools and Technologies:
The project was developed using web technologies, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and React (where implemented), along with Visual Studio Code for development and GitHub for version control and collaboration. The application is designed as a software-based educational simulation and does not require specialised hardware.

Creativity and Innovation:
The creative aspect of our project is its combination of game-based learning and simplified lunar mission simulation. Instead of only presenting information about space, it allows students to learn by making decisions and experiencing simulated mission outcomes. The junior-astronaut role, interactive challenges, resource-management activities, and mission feedback turn learning into an engaging experience.

Factors Considered:
During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, age-appropriate learning, ease of use, accessibility, engagement, and the practical limitations of a simplified simulation. We aimed to represent important lunar mission concepts responsibly without presenting the game as real astronaut training or a substitute for actual NASA mission systems. We also prioritised a clear user interface, meaningful learning outcomes, and a project that could be demonstrated effectively within the hackathon timeframe.
